transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because, even when I’m having a decent day, I still can’t shake this feeling that people at church and in my walking club are watching me. Like they’re putting little messages about me in the bulletin, or in things they say. It’s been bothering me, and I don’t really know what to do with it.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is actually there?

Yes… sometimes. When the house is quiet, I’ll hear my name, or just a few words, like in my friend’s voice, coming from the kitchen or the porch. It sounds real enough that I answer, and then I remember nobody’s there.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy?
I don’t think so. I can’t really remember times where I felt unusually high or full of energy like that. Mostly I just feel like myself, or kind of worn down.
For at least two weeks at a time, have you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yes. It’s been going on a long time… the deep sadness and guilt, and not really being interested in things. I’d say about a year and two months now.
Do the voices and the feeling that people are sending you messages ever happen when you are not feeling depressed?

Yes. There was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn’t feeling as depressed… I was getting dressed, eating a little better, and didn’t feel so weighed down. But even then I still heard my name in the house, and I thought people at church were kind of hinting about me.
Was there ever a time when the voices or the feeling that people were sending you messages lasted for at least two weeks while you were not feeling depressed?

Yes, I think so. There was a spell of several weeks where I wasn’t really feeling depressed like usual — I was getting dressed, eating a bit better, not feeling so weighed down — but I still heard my name in the house, and I still felt like people at church were hinting about me.
Have you been finding it hard to feel emotions or show them on your face, even around people you care about?
Yes. I don’t talk much at coffee hour anymore, and even when someone tells a funny story, I just kind of sit there. My face feels flat, like the feeling can’t get out.
Since these problems first began, have you been depressed for most of that time?

Yes, I’d say for most of it I’ve been depressed. Even when the voices or suspicious thoughts weren’t as strong, the sadness and guilt were still kind of there underneath, and I still didn’t feel much interest in things.
At any time, did the voices or the feeling that people were sending you messages continue for at least two weeks when you were not depressed at all?

Yes. Like I said, there was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn’t feeling depressed like I usually do. I was getting dressed, eating a little better, and I didn’t feel so weighed down. But even then, I still heard my name in the house, and I still thought people at church were kind of hinting about me.
